text:
The Minnesota Vikings have been looking for answers at safety throughout training camp, and undrafted rookie Jacob Thomas had emerged as one of the biggest surprises of the summer.

Now, his push for a roster spot has hit an unfortunate roadblock. Thomas suffered a Grade 1 ankle sprain during Friday night's preseason finale against the Denver Broncos, according to The Athletic's Alec Lewis.

Advertisement

The good news is that the diagnosis is far better than what the Vikings initially feared. A Grade 1 sprain is considered a relatively mild ankle injury, giving Thomas a realistic chance to return sooner rather than later.

Still, the timing couldn't be worse. The 22-year-old had spent the summer making a legitimate case for himself after signing with Minnesota as an undrafted free agent out of James Madison. Injuries elsewhere in the safety room opened opportunities, and Thomas consistently took advantage of them.

He wasn't simply filling snaps. Thomas was making plays.

He impressed throughout training camp, earning reps with both the first and second-team defenses and drawing praise for his instincts and ability to operate in the deep part of the field. He also recorded an interception during the preseason.

Advertisement

That momentum had put Thomas in position to potentially earn a spot on the Vikings' initial 53-man roster. And that's what makes Friday's injury so frustrating.

Minnesota is already relatively thin at safety, making Thomas' emergence even more important. The team has third-round pick Jakobe Thomas and other young options competing for playing time, but Jacob Thomas had carved out his own role through consistent production rather than draft status.

The injury doesn't erase everything Thomas accomplished this summer.

If anything, the relatively positive diagnosis gives him a chance to continue that progress once he's healthy. Thomas had done everything he could to put himself in the conversation, and ultimately, things are still leaning in his favor.

Now, the focus remains on recovering and returning at full form.

text:
The Minnesota Vikings used a top-10 pick in the 2024 NFL Draft on J.J. McCarthy, hoping he'd be their quarterback of the future. Well, McCarthy missed all of 2024 due to injury, struggled mightily in the games he was healthy enough to play in 2025, struggled in the first two preseason games, and sat out Friday's preseason finale with a minor ankle injury.

Fortunately, the injury appears to be minor, but at this point, it's fair to wonder whether McCarthy sat out so he didn't risk an injury that would've robbed Minnesota's chances of trading him. With Kyler Murray set to start and Carson Wentz outplaying him, there's every reason to believe time is up on McCarthy with the Vikings. Minnesota would certainly prefer not to cut him, meaning they might need to accept one of these mock trade proposals if they want to get anything out of him at this point.

Chargers trade package for J.J. McCarthy

The Los Angeles Chargers are set under center in 2026 and beyond with Justin Herbert, but what if Herbert were to suffer an injury? Do the Chargers really trust either Trey Lance or DJ Uiagalelei to win them a game? The answer should be a resounding no, and while McCarthy hasn't proven much at the NFL level in his own right, there's reason to believe the Chargers, in particular, would be thrilled with him as a backup.

That reason comes down to Jim Harbaugh, McCarthy's head coach at the University of Michigan. McCarthy's play under Harbaugh was so impressive that the Vikings used a top-10 pick on him. Sure, he might not ever live up to the draft billing; reuniting with his former head coach in a low-pressure environment could be for the best.

In return, the Chargers would be parting with a fifth-round pick and Trey Lance. There's reason for the Vikings to believe in Lance as their third-stringer over Max Brosmer, and while a fifth-round pick isn't much, at least it's something for a player unlikely to make Minnesota's roster, right?

Ravens trade package for J.J. McCarthy

As is the case with the Chargers, the Baltimore Ravens are set under center with Lamar Jackson now, but not only has he missed significant time due to injury, but he is also only under contract through 2027. Tyler has gone just 7-9 as a starter in the NFL, with nearly as many interceptions (10) as touchdown passes (13). Do the Ravens really trust him to take over if Jackson were to suffer an injury or to depart after next season? McCarthy might not be a clear upgrade right now, but he certainly has more upside to bet on.

Additionally, Baltimore's new head coach, Jesse Minter, was Michigan's defensive coordinator when McCarthy was there. He knows McCarthy well, giving reason to believe that he can get the most out of him. The Ravens could use more upside behind Jackson, and McCarthy has as much upside as any quarterback realistically available.

Giving up a fourth-rounder and a seventh-rounder for a quarterback who Minter knows well and was taken in the top 10 just a couple of years ago feels like a no-brainer from Baltimore's perspective, and again, while Minnesota might want more, McCarthy's value is quite low right now. This is a take what you can get sort of situation, and this is better than nothing.

Colts trade package for J.J. McCarthy

The Indianapolis Colts do not have a link to McCarthy similar to that of the Ravens and Chargers, but it's clear they could use a shake-up in their quarterback room. Much like McCarthy, Anthony Richardson has fallen out of favor with his current team after being a top draft pick, and could use a change of scenery. This deal gets that done.

The Colts would be acquiring McCarthy, giving them a quarterback to attempt to develop for the next couple of years. If they succeed, he could very well be Daniel Jones' long-term successor. If they don't, it's not like they gave up too much to acquire him.

As for Minnesota, they'd be giving Anthony Richardson a similar shot. He only has one more year left on his contract, which is why the Vikings would be giving up a slightly better pick, but who knows, maybe under Kevin O'Connell, he can find his footing at the NFL level. It's worth a shot when McCarthy is likely to be cut otherwise, right?

title: Why Drake Maye didn't play preseason; will it matter in Week 1? - ESPN
authors: Mike Reiss, Seth Walder, John Keim, NFL Nation reporters, Lindsey Thiry, Josh Weinfuss, Turron Davenport, Kevin Seifert, Todd Archer, Adam Schefter
description:
Maye-less preseason: The preseason is over, and the final starting quarterback numbers are in.
Also of note is that keeping Maye on the sideline throughout didn't appear to be Patriots coach Mike Vrabel's original intention.
Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott, for example, hasn't played in a preseason game since 2019.
Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson hasn't played in a preseason game since 2021.
Coen said a driving factor in the decision was the work Lawrence received over four joint practices with the Saints, Panthers and Buccaneers.
text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:

1. Maye-less preseason: The preseason is over, and the final starting quarterback numbers are in.

Of the league's 32 teams, 12 didn't play their established top quarterback in a game. That includes Drake Maye's Patriots and Sam Darnold's Seattle Seahawks, putting an added twist on the Super Bowl LX rematch that opens the 2026 regular season on Wednesday, Sept. 9 (NBC, 8:20 p.m. ET).

Will both quarterbacks be rusty without feeling game speed? Is the element of surprise in play more than it would have otherwise been?

Those are among the compelling questions to be answered in Seattle.

Also of note is that keeping Maye on the sideline throughout didn't appear to be Patriots coach Mike Vrabel's original intention.

When Vrabel first connected with Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken about plans for last Thursday's preseason finale, Monken shared they "had talked about initially wanting to play our starters -- get them a series or two." But Monken said both coaches ultimately came to the same conclusion: "We both felt like we were thin, especially up front on both sides of the ball. We just felt we'd be better off not playing our starters in the game."

So it was a Maye-less, starter-less preseason in New England, which Vrabel explained further late Thursday night after his backups were thumped 37-13 in a low-energy, short-week loss.

"We just wanted to try to get to the regular season with the guys that we had ... I know that's a difficult decision. I don't think there's a right or wrong answer," Vrabel said.

How teams approach the preseason with their starting quarterback is a reflection, in part, of each coach and the organizational philosophy. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott, for example, hasn't played in a preseason game since 2019. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson hasn't played in a preseason game since 2021.

Other teams that didn't have their starter play in the preseason this year include the Steelers (Aaron Rodgers), Colts (Daniel Jones), Jaguars (Trevor Lawrence), Chiefs (Patrick Mahomes), Eagles (Jalen Hurts), Lions (Jared Goff), Saints (Tyler Shough) and Rams (Matthew Stafford). In the case of the Colts' Jones and Chiefs' Mahomes, they are both returning from serious injuries sustained in 2025.

Meanwhile, Lawrence landed in a similar situation as Maye in the sense that he had played last preseason under new coach Liam Coen but was held out this preseason. Coen said a driving factor in the decision was the work Lawrence received over four joint practices with the Saints, Panthers and Buccaneers. Last year, the Jaguars had just one joint practice.

Some coaches believe those joint practices are equally as beneficial as preseason games, with teams more willing to run schemes they wouldn't in a game (when schemes would be on tape for the rest of the league to see). Another benefit is that practices are controlled, situations can be created that won't come up in a game, and quarterbacks can't be hit.

The Patriots had three joint practices (one with the Colts, two with the Eagles), and Vrabel estimated that meant about 84 full-team reps for Maye.

That was good work, but to some coaches, there's no substitute for a quarterback playing in a game when the defense can finish a sack or a hit in the pocket. Former Patriots coach Bill Belichick used to adopt that philosophy, saying at times, "You need 21 other guys out there so you can simulate football and the reactions of football."

In a decision he seemed to be wrestling with at times, Vrabel was navigating that balance with Maye and the starters this preseason.

2. Injuries mount: As the Patriots set their initial 53-man roster by Sunday's 6 p.m. ET deadline, they are dealing with a more significant injury report than they were at this time last year.

They lost No. 2 tight end Julian Hill to a season-ending knee injury in the spring, and the surefire leader for the No. 3 running back role, Terrell Jennings, was placed on injured reserve and later reached an injury settlement. Top backup interior offensive lineman Ben Brown, top swing offensive tackle Marcus Bryant and punter Bryce Baringer are candidates to be placed on IR with a designation to return.

That's one reason, along with shaky drafting before Vrabel's tenure began, that Vrabel referenced the Patriots as "not a very deep team" after the second preseason game.

Executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf noted the contrast.

"We've had some injuries here that obviously thinned things out," he said. "We were pretty lucky, knock on wood, last year with some of the injury things that we had."

3. Setting schedule: The Patriots' backups looked lethargic in Thursday's preseason finale, which wasn't entirely a surprise considering they were on the road after playing five days prior. A short week like this in the preseason from the NFL's schedule-makers seemed totally unnecessary.

Vrabel gave players three straight days off to refill their tanks, saying it might benefit everyone to get away.

They return Monday, with the next two practices set for Tuesday and Thursday. After a Friday off day, they then plan to practice Saturday, Sunday and Monday, Sept. 7, before departing for Seattle later on Monday.

That will give them a full day in Seattle on Sept. 8 before the opener.

4. They said it: "I have conversations with Christian, and I understand this is probably something that's difficult. ... Him and I communicate. Our players are always free to feel how they want to feel and you just have to stay patient and hope that we can continue to work to some sort of agreement." -- Vrabel, on cornerback Christian Gonzalez expressing frustration on contract negotiations

5. Jacas' learning curve: What does it look like when a rookie is away from the team all spring and doesn't practice until the first weekend of training camp after signing his contract late? Outside linebacker Gabe Jacas, the second-round pick from Illinois, is learning the answer to that question.

Jacas played 81 snaps over three preseason games, was attacked with regularity on read-option plays, and sometimes looked to be out of position.

Outside linebackers coach Mike Smith, who lauded Jacas for his work ethic and referred to him as "meaner than a wet mule," added context to the dynamic.

"He didn't have the spring. We do a lot on defense and so a young player like that, you're just getting him lined up, know the defense and be in the right position," he said. "Then once he masters that, it's 'what are offenses doing to you? Where are the backfield sets? How is the tackle going to set you up?' There's so much more to it, and right now he's just getting lined up."

Smith believes Jacas will be a "special player" in time.

6. Ponder thought: Second-year outside linebacker Elijah Ponder, who spent training camp as a starter opposite Dre'Mont Jones with veteran Harold Landry III on the physically unable to perform list, has won over the confidence of the coaching staff.

"Elijah has playmaking ability. He's versatile and can play multiple positions," defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr said on Boston sports radio WEEI. "I think the experience and success he had [in 2025] fed into his confidence. In joint practices, he looked like he belonged. He's going to be a big piece for the defense."

7. Hall visit: With the Patriots' final preseason game on the road against the Browns, Vrabel had the team visit the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton, Ohio as part of the day-before-game itinerary. It provided an opportunity for Patriots legend and HOFer Andre Tippett to be the tour guide.

"Having Tip be there to speak about the fraternity and his career -- he's a great Patriot. We were glad to be able to honor him in front of our football team," Vrabel said.

8. Grant's chance: Vrabel explained why he had quarterbacks coach Ashton Grant call the plays in Thursday's preseason finale.

"Ashton is a very, very good young football coach. I try to look for places to give other coaches opportunities and this was a good time," he said of Grant, 30, who had turned down an opportunity to interview for the Raiders' offensive coordinator job in the offseason to return to New England for a second year.

9. Did You Know, Part I: Wide receiver Efton Chism III and defensive tackle Jeremiah Pharms Jr. were the only players on the roster to be selected as a game captain twice during the 2026 preseason.

10. Did You Know, Part II: The Patriots will open their season in primetime for the 12th time and for the first time since the 2019 season. Of those games, four were on "Monday Night Football," four on "Thursday Night Football" and three on "Sunday Night Football."

text:
The Chicago Bears’ backups beat the Tennessee Titans’ backups last night, 24 to 15, and the NFL is done with the preseason games, so bring on Week 1 and the Carolina Panthers!

The Bears had more yards (398 to 259), more first downs (19 to 13), and led in time of possession (35:44 to 24:16). The Bears also converted 4 of 5 fourth-down attempts, while the Titans converted their only 4th-down try. Chicago was also better on third downs: 6-15 (40.0%) to 3-11 (27.3%).

The Bears were flagged 10 times for 71 yards to Tennessee’s 7 for 46 yards.

In his postgame press conference, head coach Ben Johnson said that running back Brittain Brown left the game with a concussion, and that cornerback Jaylon Jones and wideout Ray-Ray McCloud III had hamstring injuries. He also said that left tackle Ozzy Trapilo, who has yet to practice in full since being taken off the PUP list, is “right on track.” He also said that wide receiver Luther Burden III “looks 100% to me.”

Patrick Finley of the Chicago Sun-Times shared that before the game, starting corner Jaylon Johnson, “who left practice Thursday after appearing to hurt his right arm/shoulder, is doing rehab work in the end zone, throwing a heavy ball and using stretching bands.”

Running back Salvon Ahmed was kept out of the game with a minor injury, per Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune.

Before we get into some more numbers, here are all the Bears who did not play against the Titans.

And here is how the Bears started the day on both sides of the ball.

Here are the Bears’ playing time breakdowns and a few individual stats.

Offense

Tyson Bagent played the entire first half, and he went 16 of 17 for 208 yards, 2 touchdowns, and a passer rating of 156.9, with 2 runs for 21 yards. He was credited with a fumble on a bad exchange with rookie Zavion Thomas on a jet sweep, but in his postgame presser, Thomas took full responsibility for it.

Zavion had 5 catches for a game-high 140 yards, a 97-yard TD on the first play from the offense, plus a 39-yard kick return and a 22-yard punt return.

Roschon Johnson led the Bears in rushing with 15 attempts, 52 yards, and a TD.

Wideout Maurice Alexander led the Bears with 7 receptions for 50 yards and a TD. He also filled in at tailback when Brown left with a concussion, and he had 11 yards on 3 carries.

Defense

Rookie linebacker Wayne Matthews III led the defense with 6 tackles.

Linebacker T.J. Edwards, one of the few starters for the Bears who played, had 5 tackles.

Defensive end Jamree Kromah had 3 tackles, a tackle for loss, and a sack.

UDFA defensive tackle Jayden Loving had 2 tackles, 2 TFLs, a sack, a forced fumble, and a pass defended.

Corner Terell Smith had 2 passes defended.

Special Teams

*The above image has players who only played in the third phase.

Cairo Santos was 3 for 3 on extra points, and he hit his only field goal (from 37).

Tory Taylor had 2 punts and a 56 average (56 net), with 1 punt inside the twenty.

Linebacker Antonio Grier, who was just signed this week, had 3 special teams tackles plus 3 more on defense.

To check out the full Bears vs. Titans box score, ESPN has an easy-to-navigate site.

12:02 pm CT

Tom, so happy to see the chats back. What are your thoughts on players on the bubble making the 53? Kelly, Strong, Campbell, others? What about a surprise cut or two you could see? Thanks. - Tim from CA

All three of those guys are on the bubble and I could see all three making it. I think he's got a ton of upside and they have to decide whether someone else will claim him.

Do you think adding Jonnu Smith allows the Green Bay to let Musgrave go given his uncertain medical condition and pedestrian performance the last couple of years? - Mike B

Tom Silverstein

No, you don't want to give up on a second-round pick that quickly, especially at the low salary he is at. You play it out through four years because of the potential. If he's out for the season and it turns out medically it's going to be a long haul, then maybe they move on. But they don't have anyone coming down the pike with his ability, so they've got to play it out.

11:50 am CT

Why did the Packers trade Kyle McCord for a 2028 6th round draft pick. He looked so good - Mark

Tom Silverstein

They are committed to Tyrod Taylor. They want someone who has won games in the NFL and could win one in a pinch if something happens to Jordan Love. The other thing is, we don't know what weaknesses they saw in McCord. He played against some very vanilla defenses and for as much as we know, he might not be good at reading defenses. I think the Packers don't value the No. 3 as much as some do and next year's draft is full of quarterbacks, so they could find someone there.

11:44 am CT

Who else do you feel might GB South claim from among the Packers cuts?

Tom Silverstein

They might claim Jonathan Ford or Nazir Stackhouse. They need help in the middle of their defense. They need receivers, but they have young ones and so I don't think they'd be after Sturdivant. They need corners as well, but I don't see the Packers getting ready of any.

11:41 am CT

So the 6th for McCord is for the 2028 draft, not 2027?

Tom Silverstein

Bill-Atl: That is correct.

11:40 am CT

The Packers trading McCord suggests that at best they'd have cut him and hoped to resign him to the practice squad--but his performance in the Cardinals game made that unlikely. Was the Packers unloading him to the Dolphins simply a matter of getting something for nothing, i.e., they'd have lost him anyway? -- Mike D

Tom Silverstein

I think that's the case. They just weren't going to keep three guys on the active roster and they knew someone was probably going to claim him. If they were really high on him, they would have kept him as their third. They're committed to Taylor as the No. 2. They will have to add someone who can play because if Taylor gets hurt, they could be screwed.

11:27 am CT

Will the Packers likely sign a third QB to the practice squad now that McCo d has been traded?

Tom Silverstein

Yes, they absolutely have to.

11:20 am CT

Can we now officially nickname the Miami Dolphins "Packers East"? I thought they would keep McCord. A sixth round pick isn't very much but I figured that they didn't want the Bears or Vikings to pick him up if they cut him. What do you think? - Alan R

Tom Silverstein

Yes, i think we can. The pick can be considered close to a late fifth because the Dolphins are going to be terrible and could be picking first in the draft. Either way, it's at least a high 6th. It's not a premier pick, but it's probably the best they could do. And you're right, they did not want him to go to the division. The Vikings might have kept him as a third.

11:12 am CT

Packers have released WR Will Sheppard, LB Kristian Welch

Tom Silverstein

The Packers have released receiver Will Sheppard and linebacker Kristian Welch, according to sources, Ryan Wood reports.

Sheppard is coming off the exhibition final in which he scored on an 82-yard punt return. His release means the Packers have cleared the decks at receiver with one decision to make: Do they keep J. Michael Sturdivant?

Welch, a special team regular during trainiing camp, is being released. The Packers will stick with Nick Niemann as their special teams linebacker.

The Packers released another receiver: Isaiah Neyor. The big ones to watch at the position: J. Michael Sturdivant and Will Sheppard.

who becomes #3 quarterback now? - McKeough

Cut list

My colleague Ryan Wood reports that safety Murvin Kenion III has been released, per a source. I thought Kenion brought a lot of toughness to the defense and I would not be surprised if both him and Mark Perry are on the practice squad.

Hey Tom, what happened to the LB Hopper? He seemed to flash a bit the first couple of years. In the bit of preseason I watched his tackles were 3-4 yds down field. - Jeff

Yeah, that's a great question. They were kind of high on him, but he got buried on the depth chart behind Zaire Franklin and Isaiah McDuffie. 9:57 am CT

Does SILVERSTEIN RULE yet?

Tom Silverstein

Frank from PA

9:56 am CT

Is it easier to work with opposing front offices if the head coach has sla relationship with the coaching staff? For example, Matt and Mike L, Shanahan, Hafley. - M Flaiani

Tom Silverstein

You would think so. I'm sure Gutekunst and Jon-Eric Sullivan, for instance, aren't going to try to rip each other off and could have frank discussions about what they're trying to accomplish, especially since they're in different leagues. On the other hand, they play this season, so they might handle things a little closer to the vest. But Gutekunst has talked to all the GMs in the league and I'm sure has a good working relationship with many of them. 9:48 am CT

I'd keep 7 WR's, the last two being Sheppard and JMS with Savion going on IR (designated for return, thoughts?) -- Bubba

Tom Silverstein

I don't see Sheppard making it. If they're going to keep seven, it has to be Sturdivant and Savion Williams. They would essentially have eight receivers and would have to cut one when Williams came back. I'd be surprised if they did that.

9:44 am CT

Welcome back Tom! Hope you had a good off season. Prediction for starting CBs and does Gutey get a RB? -- Spero V

Tom Silverstein

I had a great off-season, thanks for asking, Spero. My prediction for starting corners is Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse with Javon Bullard in the slot. As for running backs, I'm sure he'll be on the lookout. I think they like Pierre Strong, and he has NFL experience, so they might feel OK going with him. He's a hard inside runner and a decent blocker.

9:41 am CT

Good Tom….give me some hope concerning Gannon and the defense….because i didn’t see anything in preseason at all …it looks like the same old stuff unless Gannon was holding back -- Mike

Tom Silverstein

I can't assure you that Gannon's defense will be great, but I can assure you, you didn't see it during the preseason. He ran a few blitzes against Pittsburgh but otherwise they just played vanilla scheme. He's done a ton of blitzing in training camp and he did almost none the last two games. We won't know what the defense is really going to be until about mid-season. That's how long it's going to take for them to have everything down.

9:12 am CT

Packers release tackle Brant Banks

Tom Silverstein

Ryan Wood reports per a source that tackle Brant Banks has been released.

9:11 am CT

Regarding the QB situation. After Fridays performance do the Packers risk McCord to waivers? Also, would it make sense to cut Taylor and then bring him back because I believe he’d clear waivers - Jeff Delvaux

Tom Silverstein

I think they talked about that all day yesterday. I do think you bring up a good point. They could cut Taylor instead of McCord and then re-sign him after they put someone on IR. That's a smart way to do it. There's no salary cap punishment for doing that and I doubt anybody would claim him on waivers. So, I agree, that's a pretty good idea.

9:08 am CT

What one position do you think Gutey is going to actively try and grab a player from other team to add to Pack practice squad? - Greg C in Utah

Tom Silverstein

I would think he's looking for tackles and tight ends. Everyone is looking for tackles, so that's the more difficult task. But he needs to develop another tight end. The backups he has don't seem to have big upsides.

9:06 am CT

Has there been any reporting on the length of the Gutekunst and LaFleur extension contracts? - Dan Zenner

Tom Silverstein

There has not. I have failed y'all in that regard. But I'll keep trying.

9:05 am CT

I am higher on MarShawn Lloyd than most folks. He looks very differnt this year and perhpas they really did diagnose the injury issue. Could he be RB#1 if they move on from Josh Jacobs? - Chris H.

Tom Silverstein

I don't know if Lloyd will ever be a RB 1 in the NFL. I think he could make a career of getting 15 carries and catching three or four balls out of the backfield. The durability factor would be the biggest question. But for one season, could he be the No. 1? I think so. If the Packers need him to be the No. 1 this year, they could do it. But you wouldn't want to run him into the ground. You'd have to have a complement. Kind of like what they did when it was Aaron Jones and Jamal Williams.

9:01 am CT

If Gutenkunst was going to make 1 move to upgrade the team's chances this yesr what would it be? - J. Sweat

Tom Silverstein

It would not be to acquire you. Sorry. I think he'd be looking for a better backup QB. A Malik Willis type. If there was someone on the block who could solidify the backup position, I think he'd go for it. I don't think it would be JJ McCarthy, but the kid from Pittsburgh, Will Howard, has a ton of talent and would be interesting. I don't know how he views Anthony Richardson, but he's in the same boat as Willis.

8:54 am CT

If the Packers claim a player cut from another team do they have to put that player on their 53? From what you all have reported, they could use some better O-line backup options. - Bill

Tom Silverstein

Yes, they do. And they have to remove somebody from the 53 to make room if the roster is full. I expect them to shop around for some O-line help, but there won't be much out there. A better bet would be through a trade. I could see them making a deal for a versatile veteran lineman.

8:51 am CT

The Jacobs issue may take care of itself. Does the OL have what it takes to spring Lloyd in outside zone? - Pete from East Texas

Tom Silverstein

Hey Pete, I think they'll actually be better at outside zone than inside zone. They've got some athleticism on the outside with Jordan Morgan and Zach Bako-Bewele and Banks and Monk are good on the move too. It's straight up the cut where I don't know if they'll be effective. Jacobs is good at making something out of nothing in the middle, but who knows what his status will be. I expect more outside zone this year.

8:28 am CT

Packers are releasing LS Cal Adomitis

Tom Silverstein

Per a source, the Packers are cutting long snapper Cal Adomitis. It's not a surprise but it does show that the Packers believe Matt Orzech will be ready for the season. Adomitis did a nice job and will be high on the list of replacement long snappers if he doesn't get claimed.

8:19 am CT

I agree, Tom., they have to keep Sturdivant. Cannot let him become another Taysom Hill! Do you think we will see Musgrave on the active list at any point this year? - MJ

Tom Silverstein

I'm starting to wonder if Musgrave won't be back this year. He's dealing with a neck injury. They keep saying it's going to take time to tell the severity of it. I think when you're talking about the neck and having to wait, they could be talking about a disk issue. I don't know that. I'm speculating. But if they have to operate, then he'd be done for the season I imagine. He hasn't practiced and so I think they have to put him on IR to start the season.

8:16 am CT

Do you feel Bo Melton is a lock to make the roster or could they keep Sturdivant instead if they only keep 6 wide receivers? What is the injury status of Savion Williams? - Randy B

Tom Silverstein

Yes, Melton is a lock. He can do too many things. He's one of their best special teams players, he can return kicks, he's a good fifth or sixth receiver and he can play cornerback in a pinch. No way they cut him. I don't know if Williams' ankle injury is serious, but he had an ankle that bothered him much of last season. I think they could put him on IR if they need a spot. But they only get two of those moves before the cutdown to 53, so it's questionable whether they'll use it on him. They could keep seven receivers and then make a move to IR /designated to return after the cutdown.

8:11 am CT

Is this a make or break year for Gutekunst? - John K

Tom Silverstein

Not even close. He just got a contract extension. This is probably the most talented team he's put together and he's had three straight solid drafts. He's got a load of picks next year for one of the most talent-rich drafts in a while. If you think he's a bad GM then you need to study what that really means. Go see how the Vikings managed their quarterback situation or Arizona failed to build a competitive team or Miami is absolutely devoid of talent. There is no make or break for Gutekunst. The Packers are loaded with talent. They just need to do something with it.

8:05 am CT

What are the chances Taylor is cut and we go with McCord as the lone back-up at QB? - John

Tom Silverstein

It would take some guts for them to do it, but I would if I were them. I don't know if McCord can win them a game. He looked really good in the preseason, but against the Cardinals, for instance, he didn't face much blitzing or any confusing coverages. It was pretty straightforward defense. But as I've come to learn watching 38 preseasons, the quarterbacks who can will their teams to scores like McCord did are legit. I remember watching Ty Detmer and Mark Brunell and Matt Hasselbeck and Aaron Rodgers do the same thing. If they can move the ball playing with a bunch of guys who aren't going to be in the NFL, then they've got some ability. Taylor's injury history would scare me if I were the Packers.

7:58 am CT

Good morning Tom, I hope you are more wide awake than I am. Some fans and 1 beat reporter, Huber, think the Packers should keep edge rusher Kekky. I did not read anthing about him all summer. Fill me in please. On a related note, how do the younger players develop their game during the season- do they stay after pracdtice for work. Thanks so much for doing this! ot hear a word about him all summer but now understand he has potential to be a good pass rusher but is raw. Your thoughts? On a related note, how do younger players get the help they need during the season= do they stay after poracdtice to work with coaches? -- Steve

Tom Silverstein

I agree that Kelly should be given consideration. He stepped in and showed that when he's given a lot of snaps - which he didn't receive in camp because he was an undrafted rookie -- that he can produce. Does that mean the Packers will keep him? I don't know. It's hard to get rid of big pass rushers like Kelly but obviously there are holes in his game or else he would have been drafted. The question is will they lose him if they waive him? If Collin Oliver's injury is serious enough, I'd put him on IR and keep Kelly. As for during the season, the young guys play on the scout team. They replicate the schemes the offense and defense will be facing that week. They are taught to use all the techniques the Packers teach but play a scheme that might be wildly different. They're getting a lot of snaps and that helps them develop.

7:52 am CT

Is the Sweat trade DOA? Was there ever any truth to it in the first place? - Leon

Tom Silverstein

I don't think there ever was. The Packers are in pretty good shape at edge. Lukas Van Ness had a very good camp. Now, he needs to stay healthy. Barryn Sorrell is an up and comer and I'm interested to see what he does this season. They drafted Dani Dennis-Sutton for his pass rush ability and Brenton Cox Jr. is a solid, low-cost rusher. Adding Sweat would cost them $10 million in cap space this year and $17 million next year. I just don't think it's a huge need with Parsons coming back in Week 6 or whatever.

7:47 am CT

What are some #2 QB options if the Packers move on from Tyrod Taylor? - Adam

Tom Silverstein

Good question. If they decide to cut Taylor, I could see them keeping McCord as the backup. But they would be in the market for a veteran. Pittsburgh has four quarterbacks. They're probably going to keep Mason Rudolph as the backup and rookie Drew Allar as the No. 3. That would leave Will Howard, the former Ohio State QB who played well against the Packers in Week 1 of the preseason. I won't bring up JJ McCarthy because he can't help right away. Dallas may part with either Joe Milton or Sam Howell and either of them would be an option. Stetson Bennett might not make it in LA. Andy Dalton is another veteran who may be available.

7:41 am CT

If Jordan Morgan goes down, is our best option at LT really ‘The Composer’ John Williams? - John H.

Tom Silverstein

If Jordan Morgan goes down, it will be Anthony Belton. They've purposely played him at tackle all camp long because they don't have any better options for backing up Jordan Morgan and Zach Bako-Bewele. In fact, it's not certain Bako-Bewele will be ready for opening day. But Williams is really raw and, if he makes the team, I don't see them playing him unless it's an emergency.

7:36 am CT

Good morning Tom. Hope you have plenty of coffee on hand today. I can't call today an exciting day but it is an interesting day if you are a football junkie. My question is: Do you think a UDFA will make the team this year, and if so, who do you predict it will be? - Randy

Tom Silverstein

I will be well-caffeinated, believe me. I think there are two. Receiver J. Michael Sturdivant and edge Nijalik Kelly are my two best bets to make it. I stated why Studivant should stay. Kelly is similar. He's a big man who can rush the passer and those guys don't grow on trees. He really showed something in the exhibition finale and I think he sticks. They will have to decide what to do with Collin Oliver. They could IR him, but they can only do that to two players before the cutdown to 53. And they may need those spots for Luke Musgrave and a receiver.

7:30 am CT

Q. J. Michael Sturdivant had a great game on Friday against the Cardinals and a strong preseason. Is Savion Williams put on IR so the Packers can keep Sturdivant? - Steve W.

Tom Silverstein

They have to find a way to keep Sturdivant. Guys with his kind of athleticism and improvement can't just be given away. So, they have to make a decision whether to keep seven wide receivers or make a roster move to keep him. I truly believe he'll be claimed if they let him go. They can keep seven if they go light somewhere else, say go with just three tight ends and nine offensive linemen. But if they keep the quarterback, Kyle McCord, then that eats up a space they weren't expecting to use. Williams on IR is an option.

7:22 am CT

Greetings, everybody

Tom Silverstein

Hello, everyone. Welcome to the 2026 live chat of cutdown day. I'll be here until the cuts are announced tonight to answer your questions and report any news. I've got my phone with me and will be taking some breaks to do a little reporting, so if I'm not answering questions, you'll know why. But I will return and continue with the chat until the last cut is known.

As I said in the promo, this is not the format we'll use for the regular season. Believe it or not, we finally have new software that I'm hoping will feature a much more user-friendly experience. The contract was just signed a week ago and it is being developed by our IT people. They have not given us a start date but we're putting all the pressure we can on them to be ready for Week 1.

If it's not ready, we'll find a temporary solution. It won't be this because this format doesn't work for the fast pace of a regular-season game.

Anyway, keep the questions coming and my colleague Ryan Wood and I will be working the phones in the meantime.

title: Broncos WR Marvin Mims is 'fine' after preseason injury scare
description:
It's even harder to stomach when an injury happens to a key role player like Denver Broncos wide receiver Marvin Mims.
Mims got tangled with a Vikings corner on an incomplete pass on the sideline in the first quarter, and was slow to get up.
Mims did walk to the bench under his own power, and Denver announced he was questionable to return with a foot injury.
Mims never returned to the game, and coach Sean Payton provided a positive update after a 34-6 win.
“With Mims, he’s going to be fine, it’s a bruise,” Payton said after the victory.
text:
When injuries happen in the preseason, it's always a difficult pill to swallow. It's even harder to stomach when an injury happens to a key role player like Denver Broncos wide receiver Marvin Mims.

On a night when most of the Broncos' starters didn't even dress against the Minnesota Vikings, Mims was one of the rare players who saw the field, playing on offense during the first offensive drive of the game. Mims got tangled with a Vikings corner on an incomplete pass on the sideline in the first quarter, and was slow to get up.

Mims did walk to the bench under his own power, and Denver announced he was questionable to return with a foot injury. Mims never returned to the game, and coach Sean Payton provided a positive update after a 34-6 win.

“With Mims, he’s going to be fine, it’s a bruise,” Payton said after the victory. "We were really more just cautious with him. There were a few guys we were going to get some snaps with that may have been, certainly front-line guys for us and he was one of those players.”

You can see Payton's full comments on Mims below.

Denver has 17 days from the presseason finale to their 2026 opener, a Monday Night Football matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sept. 14, which is a good window for players like Mims to heal up. In the meantime, Denver will be trimming down their roster from 91 players to the final 53-man lineup by 4:00 p.m. MST on Sunday.

title: Buffalo Bills' Injury Updates: Reason to Believe Four Key Pieces Will Be Ready Week 1
description:
It was the Buffalo Bills' preseason finale, but it doubled as a summer debut for three players working back from injuries.
WR Skyler Bell Bell has been out with a reported groin issue since August 8.
WR Keon Coleman Coleman, who was seen wearing a walking boot following the game against the Carolina Panthers, has not been practicing of late.
CB Maxwell Hairston Hairston had been sidelined since Augupst 6 due to a groin injury.
OLB Michael Hoecht Hoecht made a remarkable recovery from a mid-season Achilles tear, and he remains on track for full Week 1 availability.
text:
It was the Buffalo Bills' preseason finale, but it doubled as a summer debut for three players working back from injuries.

Veteran edge rusher Michael Hoecht, starting cornerback Maxwell Hairston and fourth-round rookie wide receiver Skyler Bell all saw their first preseason game action against the Pittsburgh Steelers on August 27. Most importantly, all three appeared to eliminate any questions about their Week 1 availability.

Meanwhile, wide receiver Keon Coleman, who tweaked his foot in the August 15 preseason opener, did not play in Thursday's preseason finale, but he also seems to be trending toward full availability for the September 13 regular season opener on the road against the Houston Texans.

Here's what we learned about all four players as the exhibition schedule came to a close on Thursday night in Orchard Park.

WR Skyler Bell

Bell has been out with a reported groin issue since August 8. The fourth-round rookie was seen doing drills with trainers as early as August 20.

After missing the first two exhibition contests, Bell started against the Steelers, and the Bills worked hard to feature him early and often.

"Try to get him involved and get the ball in his hands and allow him to go play some football. It's been awhile," said Bills' rookie head coach Joe Brady. "It wasn't too big for him, and I thought that was a huge takeaway."

Bell made a 16-yard reception on the first drive, finishing with a game-high seven catches for 49 yards. The versatile wide receiver, who totaled 52 offensive snaps, scored on a 28-yard end-around run.

WR Keon Coleman

Coleman, who was seen wearing a walking boot following the game against the Carolina Panthers, has not been practicing of late.

In a positive development, however, Coleman appeared in street clothes without the boot on Thursday night in Orchard Park. The jovial wide receiver was also seen dancing on the sideline at one point.

Presumably ready to work his way back into action, Coleman looks like he'll be fine by the season opener barring any setbacks.

CB Maxwell Hairston

Hairston had been sidelined since Augupst 6 due to a groin injury. He returned to practice in a limited capacity on August 18, but did not see game action until the August 27 finale.

"I thought it was just good for him to be just able to come out, go through it, get a feel of the environment, the game, all of that," said Brady.

Although he missed a tackle that allowed the Steelers to reach the end zone, Hairston looked fine physically while playing 15 defensive snaps. By all indications, the 2025 first-round pick is a full-go for Week 1.

"He's our starting corner. Maxwell's got exactly what we look for in a corner, and I was excited for him to be back out playing football," said Brady. "I know he had the missed tackle, that's why we're practicing. That's why you go through the preseason, to feel that, to be able to clean that stuff up."

OLB Michael Hoecht

Hoecht made a remarkable recovery from a mid-season Achilles tear, and he remains on track for full Week 1 availability.

After easing him back to speed throughout training camp, the Bills gave Hoecht his first live game reps of the summer in the finale against Pittsburgh. He started opposite second-round rookie edge rusher TJ Parker, logging 15 snaps.

"He was a captain for the game. I'm so proud of how he's handled just coming back and playing football. That's hard," said Brady.

text:
GREEN BAY (WLUK) -- NFL sources reported Thursday morning the Packers would sign former Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Jonnu Smith to the team. Just before 3:30 Saturday afternoon, Packers General Manager Brian Gutekunst made the addition official.

Thursday's reports said Smith would have a 1-year deal with the Green and Gold. No details on Smith's deal were confirmed Saturday.

Smith comes to the Packers as the team looks to add to their roster of TE options. As of Saturday, Luke Musgrave is still out due to a neck injury. ESPN's Packers depth chart lists Tucker Kraft as questionable, leaving only Josh Whyle as a guaranteed player before signing Smith.

Gutekunst also announced the Packers cut safety Tra Fluellen. He was listed 4th on the depth chart for Packers strong safety options. Previously, Fluellen signed with the New Orleans Saints as an undrafted free agent. He was selected by the Dallas Renegades for the 2026 UFL Draft. Fluellen signed with the Packers August 11.

All NFL teams must cut their rosters down to 53 players by Sunday at 6:00 p.m.

description:

text:
A strong rookie wide receiver class: Nine different rookie wide receivers appear to be among the top three wide receivers on their team based on their preseason usage, including third-round picks like Malachi Fields, Caleb Douglas and Ja’Kobi Lane.

Pick the right sleeper tight ends: Tight ends such as Chig Okonkwo emerged from the preseason with encouraging usage, while others, including Oronde Gadsden, saw more concerning roles.

365 snaps with the starters: Each team averaged more than 10 snaps with its first-team unit during the preseason, giving us a good look at how players could be used during the regular season.

Get ready for draft day with PFF Fantasy: Build your rankings with the Fantasy Rankings Builder, practice with the Mock Draft Simulator, get real-time help from the Live Draft Assistant and dig into the Fantasy Draft Kit, Fantasy Rankings and PFF Premium Stats to make every pick with an edge.

PFF's fantasy football recap focuses on player usage and stats, breaking down all the vital information you need to achieve fantasy success in 2026. This summarizes all three weeks of preseason usage in one place. If you just want the top takeaways, here are my top 10 from Week 1, Week 2 and Week 3.

With fantasy drafts happening right now, now is the time to prepare. Build your rankings with the Fantasy Rankings Builder, practice with the Mock Draft Simulator, get real-time help from the Live Draft Assistant and dig into the Fantasy Draft Kit, Fantasy Rankings and PFF Premium Stats to make every pick with an edge.

Arizona Cardinals

General

The Cardinals used their starters for 11 plays in the first week of the preseason.

QB

Jacoby Brissett played all 11 snaps with the starters.

Gardner Minshew II sat during the Hall of Fame game, was the next man up in the second game, and started the other two.

Carson Beck started the Hall of Fame game, but injuries caused him to miss the rest of the preseason.

RB

Jeremiyah Love played eight of 11 snaps with the starters, continued to play for the rest of the first half, and then missed the rest of the preseason due to injury.

Tyler Allgeier played three snaps with the starters. He continued into the second quarter but left the game before Love.

James Conner didn’t play in the preseason due to injury.

Bam Knight started the Hall of Fame game, was the next man up in the first preseason game, and sat among other key players in the other two games.

WR

Marvin Harrison Jr. played all 11 snaps with the starters.

Michael Wilson played seven snaps with the starters. Part of the reason he was substituted out may have been his receptions, but it may also signal he will play a little less.

Kendrick Bourne played eight snaps with the starters, all out of 11 personnel.

Jalen Brooks played four snaps with the starters in place of Wilson. He started the three other preseason games.

Simi Fehoko started two preseason games, entered the game after one play in a third, and was the fifth wide receiver in the first week when the starters played.

Devin Duvernay only played in Week 1 of the preseason, playing in the second quarter after Brooks and Fehoko, but his special teams play has likely earned him a roster spot.

Ihmir Smith-Marsette didn’t play in the Hall of Fame game, but was consistently the next player on the field in all three preseason games after the above players. He is likely competing with Duvernay for a roster spot.

Reggie Virgil has spent the entire preseason below the seven players above, playing until the end of the game in all four preseason games. He will likely make the roster as a fifth-round pick.

TE

Trey McBride played the first snap of the game with the starters and then his preseason was done.

Elijah Higgins missed the first three preseason games due to injury, so he played in the final game into the second quarter.

Tip Reiman spent the entire preseason on the PUP list.

Teagan Quitoriano was the next man up in each game and played only the first half.

Atlanta Falcons

General

The Falcons played 22 snaps with the starters, playing in the first quarter of the first and third preseason games.

QB

Tua Tagovailoa played all 22 snaps with the starters.

Michael Penix Jr. missed the preseason due to injury.

Cooper Rush played the first half of all three preseason games.

RB

Bijan Robinson sat out the preseason.

Brian Robinson played 20 of 22 snaps with the starters.

Tyler Goodson played two snaps with the starters. While he was below Nathan Carter on the depth chart in the first preseason game, he was clearly ahead in the other two. He stopped playing by halftime in the final two games, while Carter played into the fourth quarter.

WR

Drake London played 10 snaps with the starters. In both games, he exited before the rest of the starters, playing 100% of the snaps before leaving each game.

Jahan Dotson played all 22 snaps with the starters.

Olamide Zaccheaus played nine snaps with the starters, taking most of the 11 personnel snaps. Similar to London, he left the final preseason game early.

Zachariah Branch played four snaps with the starters, mostly after Zaccheaus left the first preseason game. He played the first half of the first game and the first quarter of the final two games.

Chris Blair played 11 snaps with the starters, all in place of London. He played the first half of all three games.

Dylan Drummond played one snap with the starters and the first half of all three games.

TE

Kyle Pitts played 17 of 22 snaps with the starters. He played 13 of 13 snaps in 11 personnel, and four of nine snaps in 12 personnel.

Charlie Woerner played nine snaps with the starters. He didn’t play in 11 personnel, but took all nine snaps out of 12 personnel.

Austin Hooper played four snaps with the starters, all in place of Pitts in 12 personnel. He also played into the second quarter of the first and third games.

Nick Muse took one snap with the starters in place of Pitts in 12 personnel. He was at the bottom of the depth chart of the first game, started the second, and played into the third quarter of the third. He would be the Falcons' fourth tight end if they keep four.

Baltimore Ravens

General

The Ravens starters didn’t play in the preseason.

QB

Lamar Jackson didn’t play in the preseason.

Tyler Huntley started all three preseason games. He played only the first quarter of the first and third games and into the second quarter of the second game.

RB

Derrick Henry and Justice Hill didn’t play in the preseason.

Rasheen Ali only played in the final preseason game due to injury. He started that game and rotated throughout the first half.

Adam Randall started the first preseason game, sat out the second, and rotated with Ali throughout the first half of the final game.

WR

Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman sat out the preseason.

Ja’Kobi Lane started the first preseason game and played into the second quarter. He only played into the second quarter of the second game, leaving before the other wide receivers. He didn’t play in the final preseason game, securing his spot as the third wide receiver.

Devontez Walker started the first preseason game, exiting at the same time as Lane. He started the second, and exited into the third quarter. He didn’t start the third game, only because Baltimore used 22 personnel, and he played the entire first half.

LaJohntay Wester played at the same time as Walker during the three preseason games, but typically only played in the slot on 11 personnel.

Chris Moore was low on the Ravens depth chart in the first preseason game, but moved up to sixth on the depth chart for the other two games, including starting in the final game.

Elijah Sarratt entered the game at 4:59 in the second quarter of the first game, 2:20 in the third quarter of the second game, and 4:11 in the first quarter of the final game. He is seventh on the depth chart at best, but will likely make the roster as a fourth-round rookie.

Xavier Guillory entered the second and third preseason games before Sarratt, suggesting he could also be in contention for a roster spot.

TE

Mark Andrews and Durham Smythe didn’t play in the preseason, suggesting Smythe will often be the second tight end in 12 personnel.

Josh Cuevas started all three preseason games. He played the entire first two games and left at halftime of the third.

Matt Hibner started all three preseason games. He played the entirety of the first two games and played into the third quarter of the third. The Ravens had only one other tight end, which is partly why the two rookies played so much.

title: Eagles worked out an intriguing edge defender; Cowboys made a weird trade | PhillyVoice

text:
NFL teams will cut down to 53 players by 6 p.m. Sunday, and we've got you covered on all the Philadelphia Eagles' cuts along the way. We'll also have analysis of the Birds' initial 53-man roster later today, and more. For now, let's briefly touch on a couple of tidbits from Saturday.

The Eagles worked out EDGE Mason Reiger

Reiger was a priority undrafted free agent who signed with the Miami Dolphins. Leading up to the draft, most analysts thought he would be selected. For example, he was Mel Kiper's 140th-ranked (4th/5th round) prospect, and Dane Brugler's 197th-ranked (5th/6th round) prospect.

But, Reiger had a complicated evaluation because of a worrisome injury history, as noted in Brugler's scouting report:

A one-year starter at Wisconsin, Reiger aligned as a wide edge rusher in defensive coordinator Mike Tressel’s four-man front. While at Louisville, he started out as Yaya Diaby’s backup before injuries took their toll. He didn’t practice for 18 months (December 2023 through June 2025) and was advised to medically retire. But he resuscitated his football career after transferring to Madison, averaging 3.8 pressures per game in 2025 (second most in the Big Ten).

Reiger doesn’t have much of a resume because of injury setbacks, but his 2025 film showed NFL-quality talent. With his linear twitch, he thrives using weaponized hands and various speed-flash moves to break down blockers. He is currently an immature finisher with too many “almost” sacks on his tape. Against the run, he gives outstanding effort, although he struggles to consistently lock out and control edges. Overall, Reiger needs to continue developing his strength, but he is an explosive athlete with promising pass-rush instincts. The medicals are an unknown variable in his draft grade and projection.

In his final season at Wisconsin, Reiger had 33 tackles and 5 sacks. He has some juice as a pass rusher. Video via @JonahTuls:

In his lone preseason game appearance, Reiger had 2 tackles and a sack, but the Dolphins waived him shortly thereafter with an injury settlement.

So, the Eagles are taking a look.

The Cowboys traded for Steelers OT Broderick Jones

As noted in our dumpster fire series this year, the Cowboys have a major concern spot at offensive tackle.

They had the No. 2 offense (yards per game) in the NFL in 2025, and honestly I don't know how they did that with the offensive tackles they were starting.

LT Tyler Guyton was the Cowboys' first-round pick in 2024. He had a bad rookie season, and then an inconsistent season in 2025 before a Week 12 ankle injury ended his season. He was replaced in the lineup by Nate Thomas, who competed with Guyton for the starting LT job this summer.

Thomas stunk in relief of Guyton last season. He is not an NFL starter. So I would guess that Brian Schottenheimer was just trying to put some pressure on Guyton to feel like he needed to win that job. But it's still not great that in Year 3 Guyton isn't already a good player, and the head coach wasn't guaranteeing his starting spot. (It became clear during camp that Guyton was the best option among the players they have on their roster.)

At RT is Terence Steele, who got paid big money after one decent season years ago but has been a well below average starter since.

The Cowboys pretty badly needed to address their tackle position in the 2026 draft, but that understandably got put on the back burner this because they had to add to their atrocious defense.

And so, with two shaky starters and virtually no depth at OT, they traded third- and sixth-round picks to the Steelers for Broderick Jones and a fourth-round pick.

That's a hefty price for tackle depth.

The Steelers had seemingly already given up on Jones, a first-round bust. I can't claim to have watched Jones in the preseason or in Steelers camp, but the overwhelming sentiment was that he had been struggling. For example, this was in the fourth quarter of a preseason game:

If I'm reading this correctly and factoring in the Jones trade, the Cowboys now only have four picks in the 2027 draft:

• Round 1: Either their own, or from GB, whichever pick is worse

• Round 2

• Round 4 (from PIT)

• Round 6

They are also not expected to receive any compensatory picks.

title: Positional Depth Decisions Complicate Bucs' Roster Cutdown - Tampa Bay Buccaneers
description:
Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell are the clear top two backs, and they are followed by Sean Tucker and Josh Williams on the depth chart.
Both Tucker and Williams originally arrived in Tampa as undrafted free agents and have since done enough to reasonably entice the Bucs to keep them on the roster.
This preseason, Williams logged 18 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown and Tucker countered with 14 totes for 50 yards and a score.
Predicting how the Bucs will handle all of these positional concerns to form that first 53-man roster by 6:00 p.m.
It is possible, of course, that the Bucs won't be able to get all of those answers before Sunday's cut deadline.
text:
With the preseason schedule complete, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers will spend the weekend trimming a 91-man camp roster down to the NFL-mandated limite of 53 players for the regular season. This is much more complicated process than simply ranking the top roster candidates from one to 53 and releasing everyone else (before bringing many of them back to the practice squad). Roster construction debates involve not only comparing one player to another, but also comparing one position to another, or several others, and deciding how to make it all fit.

To take one example almost at random, consider the Buccaneers' thought process when it comes to forming its offensive backfield. Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell are the clear top two backs, and they are followed by Sean Tucker and Josh Williams on the depth chart. Are the Bucs in the next two days choosing between Tucker and Williams for a three-man backfield, or is the actual debate whether to keep three or four, and what does that mean for the rest of the depth chart?

"That's a tough battle," said Head Coach Todd Bowles on Saturday morning following the team's loss to Jacksonville on Friday night. "It kind of went back and forth every game. Both of them can run the ball, both of them return kicks obviously, both of them try to tackle on kickoff and punt team. It's a matter of keeping four running backs, three quarterbacks; there's an extra receiver involved; obviously a corner involved, a defensive lineman. So all of that's going to be in the discussion, but that will be a tough call because they're both good football players."

Both Tucker and Williams originally arrived in Tampa as undrafted free agents and have since done enough to reasonably entice the Bucs to keep them on the roster. Tucker actually led the team with eight touchdowns last season while Williams dealt with some injuries but got some action both on offense and in the return game. This preseason, Williams logged 18 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown and Tucker countered with 14 totes for 50 yards and a score. Again, though, this is not just an exercise in comparing stat lines. It's possible that the performance of players at other positions will end up being the deciding factor when it comes to the backfield. One of those players is undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who was impressive enough in the first two preseason games to be given the bulk of the work on Friday night.

Daniels is ostensibly battling veteran Jake Browning for the primary backup spot to Baker Mayfield, but again, the larger question is whether or not there is room to keep both Daniels and Browning on the 53-man list.

"We're going to meet on it this morning and we're going to go over some things that way," said Bowles. "It's a discussion but it's not a definite. It's difficult because you probably need the spot for somewhere else, as far as [special] teams or an extra rusher or an extra back or an extra offensive lineman. Knowing that guy's not going to play [except] in case of emergency, I think every position would like to have insurance behind the insurance. It's something you've got to weigh the pros and cons of and make that decision going forward."

Predicting how the Bucs will handle all of these positional concerns to form that first 53-man roster by 6:00 p.m. ET on Sunday is particularly difficult without access to the team's complete health situation. For instance, the status of wide receivers Jalen McMillan (knee) and Emeka Egbuka (toe) could definitely impact that Week One roster construction. Just a year ago, the Buccaneers opened the season with seven receivers on the active roster because Chris Godwin was not placed on injured reserve but he was also not ready to go for the first three weeks. That situation could repeat itself this week, which in turn could mean a lighter depth chart at quarterback, running back, defensive back, defensive line or offensive line.

"It's been a question that we've got to answer," said Bowles. "It's one of them, but we expect J-Mac and hopefully Emeka to come back before Week One and be at full strength that way. That will have a lot to do with whether we keep the extra one or not, and how healthy these guys are going forward."

It is possible, of course, that the Bucs won't be able to get all of those answers before Sunday's cut deadline. Regardless they will have to decide how the first 53 are arranged, and it won't be as simple as deciding one player is better than another.

title: Court: Former Washington Commanders player can get workers' comp for training camp injury
authors: Valerie Bonk, William J. Ford, Maryland Matters, The Associated Press
description:
A former Washington Commanders football player who ruptured his Achilles tendon during training camp in 2023 is entitled to workers’ compensation benefits for the injury, the Appellate Court of Maryland ruled this week.
According to the 20-page ruling, Brooks never made it on the Commanders’ active roster and didn’t play a game.
Brooks appealed to the county circuit court, which held a hearing on May 6, 2025.
And at the time, on August 6 of 2023, he [Brooks] was an employee of this football team.
But he was cut by the Titans in July, during preseason camp, and signed by the Commanders in August of that year.
text:
This article was republished with permission from WTOP’s news partners at Maryland Matters. Read the story at Maryland Matters.

A former Washington Commanders football player who ruptured his Achilles tendon during training camp in 2023 is entitled to workers’ compensation benefits for the injury, the Appellate Court of Maryland ruled this week.

The Wednesday ruling upheld an earlier Prince George’s County Circuit Court decision that said Curtis Brooks, who signed with the team Aug. 3, 2023, to play on the defensive line, was a “covered employee” when his injury happened three days later during an early training camp practice.

According to the 20-page ruling, Brooks never made it on the Commanders’ active roster and didn’t play a game.

But the terms of his contract at the time said it “covers 1 football season(s), and will begin on the date of execution, and end on the last day of the 2023 League Year, unless extended, terminated, or renewed as specified elsewhere in this contract.”

In terms of injury, another part of the contract states, “Unless this contract specifically provides otherwise, if Player is injured in the performance of his services under this contract and promptly reports such injury to the Club physician or trainer, then Player will receive such medical and hospital care during the term of this contract.”

Brooks, who hasn’t played in the National Football League since his injury, filed a worker’s compensation claim with the Maryland Workers’ Compensation Commission in March 2024. Two months later, the commission rejected his claim, saying Brooks did not qualify as a covered employee in the state and that the injury occurred at a practice at the team’s training facility in Ashburn, Virginia.

Brooks appealed to the county circuit court, which held a hearing on May 6, 2025.

The circuit court reversed the commission decision, writing that all players’ primary employment and home games with the Commanders in the National Football League are at Northwest Stadium in Prince George’s County.

A three-judge panel with the Appellate Court – Judge Stuart R. Berger who wrote the opinion, and Judge Rosalyn Tang and Senior Judge James A. Kenney III – affirmed the county Circuit Court’s decision.

In an email Friday, a team official said the Commanders would not be commenting on the case. Representatives with the workers’ comp commission did not respond to requests for comment.

According to the court document, Rob Rogers, the Commanders senior vice president of football operations, testified in circuit court that Brooks likely would have played in two preseason games in Maryland, but he “likened the games to a tryout.”

But when asked directly by Brooks’ attorney, “At no time before Mr. Brooks signed his contract, did you tell him that you did not think he was going to make the team, did you?” Rogers replied, “No.”

The circuit court entered a verbal ruling for Brooks on May 13, 2025.

In part, the court said, “This is just a contract for a season. And at the time, on August 6 of 2023, he [Brooks] was an employee of this football team. And quite honestly, there was an argument about, well, you know, ‘consistent and predictable.’ But what this contract says is that he is employed by the Commanders for the 2023 NFL season.”

On appeal to the Appellate Court of Maryland, the Commanders focused on the fact that Brooks was injured in Virginia, and that his employment with the team “was not consistent and predictable” because he had only been with the team for three days prior to his injury “and was not likely to play games in Maryland on a consistent and predictable basis.”

But Berger wrote that the team “invites us to engage in speculation regarding how many games Mr. Brooks would have played in Maryland to determine whether Mr. Brooks would have been covered. We decline to engage in such speculation. Indeed, effectively establishing a certain number of games that would meet the threshold for ‘regular’ and ‘predictable’ employment is an inexact estimation.”

Brooks finished his collegiate career in 2021 at the University of Cincinnati as a defensive tackle and an All-American Athletic Conference First Team honoree. He was drafted in the sixth round in 2022 by the Indianapolis Colts.

He was transferred to the Colts’ practice squad and then released in December 2022 before signing with the Tennessee Titans practice squad in January 2023. But he was cut by the Titans in July, during preseason camp, and signed by the Commanders in August of that year.

title: Luther Burden Trending Towards a Return from Injury in Time for Week 1 - Sports Illustrated
description:
It's been a rough summer for the Chicago Bears in terms of training camp injuries.
The offense has been hurt too, with Luther Burden III dealing with a groin injury he suffered early in training camp.
The Bears should not rush Luther Burden back from injury While this is the second positive injury update on Burden in just the past week, I wouldn't act too rashly if I were the Chicago Bears' coaching staff.
Two-time Pro Bowl cornerback Jaylon Johnson injured his groin during a private workout in July and missed all of training camp.
Bears' season depends on Luther Burden having a breakout season Despite a wildly successful 2025 season, the Bears are not content to rest on their laurels.
text:
It's been a rough summer for the Chicago Bears in terms of training camp injuries. Free agency acquisition Coby Bryant's injury became a worst-case scenario earlier this month, sidelining him for four to six months, and Kyler Gordon still hasn't taken a single snap, despite starting training camp on the PUP list (Physically Unable to Perform).

The offense has been hurt too, with Luther Burden III dealing with a groin injury he suffered early in training camp. While he avoided a major injury, the news was still a mixed bag for the Bears as Burden has missed most of training camp and all three preseason games. However, he appears to be trending in the right direction and may be ready for Week 1.

According to Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune, Burden was "moving well" as he ran some routes ahead of the Bears' final preseason game. "Maybe not 100%, but he's running routes and getting in and out of his breaks," Biggs said on X. "That bodes well for potential Week 1 availability two weeks from tomorrow."

The Bears should not rush Luther Burden back from injury

While this is the second positive injury update on Burden in just the past week, I wouldn't act too rashly if I were the Chicago Bears' coaching staff. If he's still not 100% in two weeks, I would say to let him rest. Burden may be a critical component of Ben Johnson's offense and the expectant WR1 on the Bears' depth chart, but the Bears could afford to go one game without him, especially in Week 1 against a vulnerable opponent like the Carolina Panthers.

Alternatively, if the Bears try to rush Burden back before he's fully healed, they risk the same catastrophic scenario they saw last year. Two-time Pro Bowl cornerback Jaylon Johnson injured his groin during a private workout in July and missed all of training camp. He tried to make his season debut in Week 2 but reinjured himself and was ruled out indefinitely.

I would hope that Johnson's disappointing 2025 campaign would serve as a cautionary tale for the Bears regarding Burden. Groin injuries can be tricky, and even when Johnson was on the field last year, he was clearly nowhere close to the best version of himself. It'd be far better for the team to go without Burden in Week 1 than to miss him for the next 10 weeks, if that's what it comes down to.

Bears' season depends on Luther Burden having a breakout season

Despite a wildly successful 2025 season, the Bears are not content to rest on their laurels. They have big plans for the 2026 season, and head coach Ben Johnson intends to break the 2013 Broncos' NFL scoring record. If they're going to have any chance of achieving this goal, the Bears will need as close to a full season of Luther Burden as they can get.

Burden's speed and explosive playmaking ability after the catch make him a true homerun threat every time he steps on the field. He showed flashes of brilliance last year as a rookie, and those flashes should become trends now that he has a full year of experience in Ben Johnson's offense under his belt. Rome Odunze might still have a breakout season of his own, but he's not the kind of electric playmaker that Burden is.

If Burden hits his ceiling in 2026, that will likely mean that Caleb Williams has ended Chicago's 106-year streak without a 4,000-yard passer, and the Bears will almost certainly repeat as NFC North division champs, assuming the defense can hold up their end of the bargain.

text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have traded offensive lineman Broderick Jones to the Dallas Cowboys, according to NFL insider Adam Schefter. The Steelers will also reportedly send a fourth-round draft pick to Dallas in exchange for third- and sixth-round picks.

Jones, 25, was Pittsburgh's first-round pick, 14th overall, in the 2023 NFL draft. He previously played three seasons of collegiate football at Georgia. Jones has 38 career starts in the NFL.

Jones was placed on injured reserve in November 2025 with a neck injury, causing him to miss the remainder of last season.

The Steelers selected offensive tackle Max Iheanachor with the team's first-round pick when Pittsburgh hosted the NFL draft in April.

Steelers general manager Omar Khan said that Jones' injury was a factor in the decision to draft Iheanachor.

"Sure, that's a little bit of a concern," Khan said at the time. "You guys all hear me talk about versatility too, and we've got guys on the offensive line that can play different positions in the offensive line. And as I mentioned, we have options."
